text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- United Nations officials say they have "consistent and absolutely credible" reports supporters of deposed Cambodian First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh had been tortured after his ouster by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
- Fecent evacuation of 450 Singaporeans from Phnom Penh by Singapore Armed Forces demonstrates how "totally competent and well organised" it is, Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong says.
- Prince Norodom Ranariddh arrives in Singapore on Sunday and will hold talks with Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong on Monday.

- Malaysian influence over South Pacific countries increasing as its timber firms help prop up some regional rulers, while other states look to Kuala Lumpur to counter Australian dominance, secret Australian government report warns.

- Singapore companies' chances of getting long-delayed S$640 million international airport project in Banglalore off the ground still very much "alive", says India's new Civil Aviation Secretary M.S. Kaw.
- There is no rethinking on Singapore Airlines' proposed joint venture with India's Tata group for new domestic airline in country.

- Toubled mainboard-listed CAM International Holdings takes legal action against former executive chairman Raymond Chew and three others over S$1.45 million payment made by its subsidiary to local company.
- Turned off by weak market returns and overvalued currencies, U.S fund managers treat stock markets in most of Southeast Asia with indifference or even outright fear so far this year.
- New York, London and other global share markets expected to be nervous this week following an unexpected 130-point slide on Wall Street on Friday, dealers say.
- Singapore's Big Four banks pushing hard to expand overseas, but it's proven to be hard going.
- DBS Bank could be sitting on paper profit of at least S$56 million for its investment in office and commercial property project in Admiralty business district in Hongkong.
